item.text: {"question_id":"3B.7","answer":"In 2023, China maintained extensive formal protection frameworks for women, children, and other vulnerable groups. The women’s-rights law required government coordination, budget inclusion, complaint handling, protection from violence and trafficking, sexual-harassment procedures, legal aid, hotlines, supervisory correction, and penalties for retaliation or official failure; child-protection law required budgeted government protection systems and timely handling of reports, while the online-minor regulation was adopted and promulgated in 2023 but took effect in 2024 (BATCH-0021-E010; BATCH-0021-E011; BATCH-0021-E013; BATCH-0024-E010; BATCH-0021-E003). Administrative evidence also records national medical-assistance and insurance coverage and education spending, but these aggregates do not establish protection from targeted violence, equitable access, service adequacy, or Xi-specific causation (BATCH-0016-E009; BATCH-0013-E006). Implementation and outcomes were materially unequal and often ineffective. Domestic violence remained widespread, authorities often failed to enforce protections, victims faced difficulty obtaining accountability, and assistance did not always reach survivors (BATCH-0001-E011; BATCH-0010-E025). Minority communities faced coercive population-control measures, detention, assimilation, discrimination, forced relocation, and reduced access to education and employment; Human Rights Watch reported that approximately half a million Uyghurs and other Turkic Muslims remained imprisoned, while an OHCHR communication recorded allegations of widespread Uyghur child-family separation, without establishing a personal order by Xi or a final adjudicative finding (BATCH-0001-E011; BATCH-0001-E012; BATCH-0010-E024; BATCH-0011-E008). LGBT organizations and accounts were closed or censored, although the supplied evidence does not directly establish central orders for each closure (BATCH-0010-E026). Disability protection was constrained by certification barriers, low and locally variable benefits, weak civil-society participation, rural and migrant access gaps, and reported official dereliction; the evidence is mainly structural or pre-2023 rather than a complete 2023 measurement (BATCH-0026-E015; BATCH-0026-E016; BATCH-0026-E018). The Feng County case illustrates severe local failure to prevent trafficking and prolonged abuse of a woman with a disability, followed by 2023 prosecutions; it demonstrates post-harm remedy, not effective nationwide prevention (BATCH-0026-E018). Local Deqin assistance outputs are retained only as limited contextual evidence of implementation, not as proof of national ruler-level protection or equitable access (BATCH-0020-E001; BATCH-0020-E002; continuation during 2023 is documented for some items.","The OHCHR child-separation item is an allegation recorded in a communication, identifies one alleged victim in the supplied summary, and does not establish scale, responsible officials, or government response.","The half-million detention estimate lacks a complete denominator or case list, and the supplied evidence does not establish a personal Xi order.","Disability-registration, benefit, rural-access, and healthcare evidence is mainly from 2021–2022 or selected jurisdictions and cannot provide a complete 2023 national outcome.","The Feng County prosecutions show institutional remedy after severe harm but do not establish prevention or nationwide enforcement.","Local Deqin outputs cannot be generalized to national policy or attributed personally to Xi without evidence of central direction, funding conditions, monitoring, or scalable implementation.","The record does not provide complete geographically or population-disaggregated outcomes for women, children, minorities, migrants, disabled people, LGBT people, or other vulnerable groups."],"corrections_made":["Removed aggregate health, education, and local assistance figures as substantive proof of targeted-violence protection or equitable national access; retained them only with explicit limitations.","Added the omitted OHCHR child-family-separation evidence and the women’s-rights accountability evidence.","Added the Feng County case as post-harm remedy and local protection failure, without treating prosecution as proof of prevention.","Corrected attribution limits for local Deqin assistance, LGBT account closures, disability programs, and national administrative outcomes.","Preserved the distinction between formal safeguards, implementation, outcomes, severity, remedy, temporal fit, and ruler-specific causation.","Corrected the online-minor regulation’s period by noting its 2024 effective date."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A score-bearing judgment would require the full ruler-period ledger, calibrated cross-ruler comparison, and explicit assessment of whether the documented minority abuses constitute systematic repression or a higher severity class.","Further review could materially change the assessment if stronger evidence establishes the scale, command responsibility, prevention failures, or remedies concerning child-family separation, Xinjiang detention, trafficking, or regional access disparities.","The supplied record is incomplete for equitable access and for direct personal attribution to Xi, especially outside formal national policy." ]}
